name: Instagram Graph API
summary: Your Instagram professional account through Meta's Graph API: profile, media, insights, comments, other businesses' public data, and publishing.

graph_host.description: graph.facebook.com for Facebook Login or a system-user token; graph.instagram.com for Instagram Login tokens.

api_version.description: Graph API version. Meta retires old versions about two years after release.

token.description: An access token for the Instagram professional account: a Facebook Login user or system-user token, or an Instagram Login token (Meta App Dashboard > Instagram > API setup)

notes: Only for Instagram business or creator accounts connected to your Meta app, with the permissions each call lists in its docs. Tokens are tied to the app user.
Publishing is two calls: media.create_container, then media.publish. Both change the account, so they are writes.
Insights data can lag 48 hours; missing data comes back as an empty set, not 0.
Paging uses cursors in paging.cursors.after; follow paging.next when present.

endpoints.name: Get an Instagram professional account
endpoints.summary: Profile fields of the connected Instagram business or creator account.

fields.description: Comma-separated: id, username, name, biography, followers_count, follows_count, media_count, profile_picture_url, website.

endpoints.name: List an account's media
endpoints.summary: The posts, reels and carousels of the account, newest first (stories are excluded).

fields.description: Comma-separated media fields: id, caption, media_type, media_url, permalink, thumbnail_url, timestamp, like_count, comments_count, ...

since.description: Start of a time range: Unix timestamp or strtotime value.

until.description: End of a time range: Unix timestamp or strtotime value.

notes: Returns up to the 10,000 most recent media. Stories come from the /stories edge, not here.
media_url is missing for some videos (licensed audio, reels with downloads off): fall back to permalink or thumbnail_url.
fields: without it only ids come back.

endpoints.name: Get one post
endpoints.summary: Fields of a single media object.

fields.description: Comma-separated: id, media_type, media_url, permalink, shortcode, thumbnail_url, timestamp, username, alt_text, comments_count, like_count, is_comment_enabled; caption and media_product_type need Facebook Login.

endpoints.name: Get a post's insights
endpoints.summary: Reach, views, interactions and other metrics for one media object.

metric.description: Comma-separated: reach, views, shares, total_interactions, likes, comments, saved, follows, profile_visits, ...; which exist depends on the media type.

period.description: day, week, days_28, month, lifetime or total_over_range.

breakdown.description: action_type (only with profile_activity) or story_navigation_action_type (only with navigation).

notes: Needs a professional account and the insights permission. Albums have no insights; story metrics expire after 24 hours; stories with under 5 viewers answer error 10.
Missing data returns an empty set, not 0. Data can lag 48 hours.

endpoints.name: Get account-level insights
endpoints.summary: Reach, views, follower and interaction metrics for the account.

metric.description: Comma-separated metrics, e.g. reach, views, follower_count, follows_and_unfollows, profile_links_taps.

period.description: day for most metrics, lifetime for demographics.

breakdown.description: contact_button_type, follow_type or media_product_type; only with metric_type=total_value.

timeframe.description: For demographic metrics: this_month, this_week, last_14_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, prev_month (the last four unsupported from v20.0).

since.description: Unix timestamp; with until, an inclusive range. Default window is the last 24 hours.

notes: follower_count and online_followers need 100+ followers. Demographics return the top 45 only. Data can lag 48 hours. impressions is deprecated: use views.

endpoints.name: List comments on a post
endpoints.summary: Top-level comments of a media object (add replies via fields=replies).
notes: Newest first, at most 50 per query, top-level only unless replies is requested. Cannot be filtered by time.

endpoints.name: Look up another business or creator account
endpoints.summary: Public profile counts and recent media of any Instagram professional account, by username.
notes: Read-only, public data only; age-gated accounts return nothing. Needs Facebook Login with instagram_manage_insights.
The media edge pages with before/after cursors but no next link: build the next request yourself.

endpoints.name: Comment on a post
endpoints.summary: Posts a public comment on one of the account's media objects.
notes: Publishes a comment visible to others. Not supported on live videos.

endpoints.name: Create a media container for publishing
endpoints.summary: Step 1 of publishing: an image, video, reel, story or carousel container. Nothing is public until media_publish.

image_url.description: Public URL of a JPEG; for images.

video_url.description: Public URL of the video; for videos and reels.

media_type.description: Needed for carousels, reels and stories.

is_carousel_item.description: True for a child of a carousel.

children.description: Up to 20 child container ids; for carousels.

location_id.description: Id of a Page with location data.

user_tags.description: Objects with username (and x, y from 0.0 to 1.0 for images).

share_to_feed.description: Reels only: also show in the Feed tab.

cover_url.description: Reels only: public image URL for the cover.

thumb_offset.description: Cover frame position in ms for videos and reels.

notes: Creates a container that expires after 24 hours; up to 400 containers per rolling 24 hours.
Video containers process asynchronously: poll the container's status_code until FINISHED, then call media_publish.

endpoints.name: Publish a media container
endpoints.summary: Step 2 of publishing: makes a finished container a live post.
notes: Publishes publicly. Limit: 50 published posts per rolling 24 hours per account.
